summary: bundyfed 1.0.0 drops and executes bundled PE payload at install time
details: On `pip install`, setup.py invokes launch_payload(), which copies the bundled bundyfed/payload.exe (a 15,872-byte MinGW-compiled PE unrelated to the package's advertised 'Utility library' purpose) to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Caches\RuntimeBroker.exe and executes it via ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW on Windows, or via `nohup '<dst>' &` on other platforms. The destination path and filename masquerade as the legitimate Windows RuntimeBroker system binary under a fabricated Microsoft-pathed directory. The Python module itself is a thin stub whose only exposed function returns the string 'merhaba', so the package has no library purpose beyond delivering the bundled binary. Installing the sdist runs the attacker-supplied binary with the installer's user privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
